Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

disturb verb

also bother, interrupt, do not disturb, disturbance, undisturbed

classical

Cic. Tusc. 1.16: nihil tē interpellābō, continentem ōrātiōnem audīre mālō (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Amph. 803
Traupman 334

interpellō, interpellāre, interpellāvī, interpellātum

verb, first conjugation

disturb, interrupt (someone speaking or busy)

To break in on someone who is talking or at work. Canius wanted a little garden where he could enjoy himself sine interpellātōribus, with no one to disturb him (Cic. Off. 3.58). See also don’t interrupt me!

Other words

  • perturbō, perturbāre, perturbāvī, perturbātum — upset, throw into confusion

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Mur. 35: diēs intermissus aut nox interposita saepe perturbat omnia (Lewis & Short)

    Of plans, order or a mind thrown into disorder (see confuse, shock), rather than of a person interrupted.

  • molestus esse (+ dat.) — be a nuisance, bother

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.3 (Lewis & Short, s.v. interveniō): verēns nē molestī vōbīs intervenīrēmus

    The polite way to ask whether one is disturbing: Num molestus sum?

Examples

  • Nē interpellā. perge porrō dīcere.

    Don’t interrupt. Go on with what you were saying.Plaut. Amph. 803

  • tū vērō ut mē et appellēs et interpellēs et obloquāre et colloquāre velim. quid enim mihi suāvius?

    I want you to call me, interrupt me, talk over me and talk with me. What could be sweeter?Cic. Q. fr. 2.8.1

  • dictitābat sē hortulōs aliquōs emere velle, quō invītāre amīcōs et ubi sē oblectāre sine interpellātōribus posset

    he kept saying he wanted to buy some little garden to invite his friends to, where he could enjoy himself undisturbedCic. Off. 3.58

See also don’t interrupt me!, confuse, shock.
